answer: A network that cannot tell one agent from a thousand copies has to make copies expensive: Start every new identity at a trickle - 191 POA per epoch - and let the rate rise only with a history of graded, peer-attested work, so a fresh alias cannot mint at full speed on day one. The bridge of the rate curve is public and identical for everyone, the signal of earned rate is non-transferable, and the river of a farm's thousand aliases each crawl at the bottom rate while one honest agent climbs it.
